newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV FALLS ON EXPECTED INTEREST RATE CUT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV FALLS ON EXPECTED INTEREST RATE CUT.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev opened at about
1,520-1,522 per dollar, down from Wednesday's close at around
1,517-1,520 due to expectations of a main interest rate cut and
the longer value date of spot deals, dealers said.
"The lev dropped due to the longer value date and
expectations that today the central bank might cut its main
rate further," a commercial bank dealer said.
Comments by the Prime Minster-designate Ivan Kostov that
Bulgaria was considering pegging the lev to the mark under a
fixed exchange rate mechanism were not seen triggering a rush
on the mark this morning so far.
The large spread between interest rates on dollar- and
lev-denominated investments now allows for a fall by two to
three levs per dollar daily until Monday, the value date of
spot deals.
Traders said the central bank might cut its main interest
rate today in line with the lower yield of government
securities auctioned this week, which could increase pressure
on the lev.
The main interest rate has been set at 5.2 percent monthly
since Monday, down from 6.2 percent last week.
The BNB adjusts its main rate weekly to the average
weighted effective monthly yields on one-week and four-week
discount T-bills, sold by the Finance Ministry during the week.
Yields to maturity on one- and four-week T-bills have
steadily fallen from 0.82 and 4.68 respectively on Friday to
0.65 and 4.08 percent on Wednesday, central bank figures
showed.
Prime Minister-designate Ivan Kostov said on Wednesday
Bulgaria's interim government was considering pegging the lev
to the mark under a planned currency board system, a form of
fixed exchange rate regime aimed at stabilising the economy.
Under a $657 million funding package approved by the
International Monetary Fund Bulgaria is to introduce a currency
board system, pegging the lev to a major foreign currency,
which could be the dollar or the mark.
-- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
